column1: # Auralis canonical parameter table — THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH
# Every module implementation, the UI panel, the preset writer, the plugin
# adapter and the docs generator read this file.  Do not fork it.
# Format (tab separated, 17 columns, every data row has all 17):
#   code  display_name  category  edition  element  param  type  default
#   min  max  curve  exponent  unit  choices  group  help  aliases
# Lines starting with '#' are comments; blank lines ignored.
# default/min/max are in NATURAL units (dB, Hz, ms, %, st). The UI maps to 0..1.
#   * unit      : the unit the module actually works in ("" when the value is
#                 a plain ratio).  A frequency is always in Hz, a level in dB
#                 (dBFS when it is measured against full scale), a time in ms
#   * choices   : the strings of an enum, separated by "|", in the order the
#                 module expects them.  Empty for every other type.
#   * min / max : the domain of a float or an int.  For an enum they are the
#                 0-based index range of the choices: 0 .. len(choices) - 1.
#   * curve     : the law the travel of the parameter follows.
#                   linear  a straight line between min and max.  A threshold
#                           is judged against the signal, not against unity,
#                           so a threshold stays on a straight line.
#                   log     a straight line in the logarithm of the value.
#                           Every hertz parameter whose range starts above zero
#                           uses it, so that one percent of the travel moves
#                           the frequency by the same number of octaves at the
#                           bottom of the range as at the top.
#                   taper   v = lo + (hi - lo) * n ** p, the shape of a gain
#                           fader: a wide cut, a narrow boost, unity in the
#   * exponent  : the p of the taper law.  It is carried beside the range
#                 because the shape belongs to the parameter, not to the law.
#   * help      : the sentence that says what the parameter does.  It is the
#                 same sentence the module publishes for the parameter.
#   * aliases   : the names the parameter had before it was renamed, separated
#                 by "|".  A document that carries an old name still loads and
#                 the old name is still accepted.
#   * the id of a parameter is its position inside its own module, so a
#     parameter is appended at the end of its module's block.  Removing one
#     in the middle renumbers the ones after it; the hole that would avoid
#     that is an open question (var/patches/f1_open_questions.md, Q3).
# Shared parameter names are reused verbatim across modules so the UI can offer
# consistent tooltips and the preset layer can be generic.  One word names one
# idea: the amount that is taken out of a signal is a Reduction, a level
# applied to a source is a Gain, a level at which a module starts to act is a
# Threshold and how eagerly a detector reacts is a Sensitivity.
